_probe: Does a timeframe-inert (bundle-read) metric accept a column-level timeframe other than {rel:'anchor'}?
_why: omega/validate.py enforced the timeless rule only at SECTION level (a section carrying a `timeframe` override). The column's OWN timeframe was never checked, so omega accepted three shapes the platform refuses. Found while searching for REGIME_MOM's rule - the search needed REGIME_MOM at the regime timeframe and the platform refused to render it.

probes.message: [column-grammar] metric 'regMom' is timeframe-inert (a bundle read) - it accepts only the anchor timeframe reference, not 'lower'
[column-grammar] metric 'regMom' is timeframe-inert (a bundle read) - it accepts only the anchor timeframe reference, not 'regime'

[column-grammar] metric 'regMom' is timeframe-inert (a bundle read) - it accepts only the anchor timeframe reference, not '1h'
probes.significance: THE DECIDING PROBE. The anchor IS 1h, so this resolves to exactly the anchor timeframe and is still refused. The constraint is syntactic, not semantic: the column timeframe must be the literal reference {rel:'anchor'}, not merely something equal to it. Inferring the rule from the 'regime' message alone would have produced a validator that wrongly passes {abs:<anchor>}.

rule: A metric with timeframeMode == 'timeless' accepts exactly one column timeframe: {"rel": "anchor"}. Every other rel, and every abs - including an abs equal to the anchor - is refused with REPORT_COLUMN_CONSTRUCTION_FAILED. The error's allowedDomain lists 'offset' as the only remaining free column parameter.

affectedMetrics.note: every metric whose timeframeMode is 'timeless'; omega previously accepted a non-anchor column timeframe on all of them
